p.note: Lycormas fl. Ovid. Met. lib. 2. Luc. lib. 12. Virg. Æn. lib. 1. Gargara mons. Seneca in Thebaide.
p.i: Inscius in sicco serpentem puluere riuum
Ardentésque auertit equos in castra prius, quàm
Hinc grata Cereri Gargara, & dives solum,
Quod Xanthus ambit niuibus Idæis tumens.
Hinc, quà relinquit nomen Ionij maris,
Aut quà latus iam propior orienti dedit,

main_text.head: Mæander & Marsia fl. in Phrygia oriuntur.

p.i: Quà celer & rectis descendens Marsya ripis
Quíque recuruatis Ludit Mæander in undis.

main_text.head: Simois fl.
main_text.p: Claudian. de laud. Stili. lib. 1. Idem de raptu Proserp. lib. 3. Virg. Æn. lib. 1. Scamander idem qui & Xanthus fl. Horat. in Epodis.Non sic intremuit Simois, cùm montibus Ida Nigra coloratus produceret agmina Memnon. Tollebant gemina capita inuiolata cupressus Cespite vicino: quales non rupibus Idæ Miratur Simois: quales non diuite ripa Lambit Apollinei nemoris nutritor Orontes. Túne ille Æneas, quem Dardanio Anchisæ Alma Venus Phrygij genuit Simoentis ad vndam? Te manet Assaraci tellus: quam frigida parui Findunt Scamandri flumina, lubricus & Simois. Æ Q-

page.notes: Marginal notes are reproduced in the left margin as printed. Some words in the notes and the catchword line at the foot are faint; the bottom "Æ Q-" is a partial catchword and is uncertain. Several verse words in the main text are doubtful due to print quality.
